title: Sample-efficient and Scalable Exploration in Continuous-Time RL
claim: Our uncertainty-driven exploration reaches near-optimal returns quickly, while baselines plateau lower or fail on harder tasks.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, shared y-axis, dashed optimal reference line
description: Two side-by-side line plots of normalized average episode return against episode number. The left panel, titled 'Pendulum-GP: Swing-up', runs to about 12 episodes. The right panel, titled 'Mountaincar-GP: Go up', runs to 15 episodes. A black dashed horizontal line at 1.0 marks the optimal return under true dynamics. A bold red solid curve is the proposed method, with a light red shaded band for standard error. Blue dotted, green dash-dot and purple dashed curves are baselines with matching shaded bands. On the left, all methods climb quickly to about 0.8, and red ends slightly higher at about 0.9. On the right, red rises to about 0.85 within a few episodes. The baselines stay near zero, apart from green reaching about 0.2 and blue about 0.3 late. The eye goes first to the red curve. Gray gridlines run behind the curves.
caption: GP dynamics. Learning curves for baselines, \combrl and OCORL with fixed internal reward weight $\lambda_n$ using GP dynamics and iCEM planning, averaged over 5 seeds. We report the mean and the standard error bands, and additionally the performance of MPC under the true dynamics as an estimate for the performance of the optimal policy. \combrl achieves higher asymptotic returns than PETS and mean, while matching or exceeding OCORL at roughly $3\times$ lower computational cost (Appendix [ref]).
abstract: Reinforcement learning algorithms are typically designed for discrete-time dynamics, even though the underlying real-world control systems are often continuous in time. In this paper, we study the problem of continuous-time reinforcement learning, where the unknown system dynamics are represented using nonlinear ordinary differential equations (ODEs). We leverage probabilistic models, such as Gaussian processes and Bayesian neural networks, to learn an uncertainty-aware model of the underlying ODE. Our algorithm, COMBRL, greedily maximizes a weighted sum of the extrinsic reward and model epistemic uncertainty. This yields a scalable and sample-efficient approach to continuous-time model-based RL. We show that COMBRL achieves sublinear regret in the reward-driven setting, and in the unsupervised RL setting (i.e., without extrinsic rewards), we provide a sample complexity bound. In our experiments, we evaluate COMBRL in both standard and unsupervised RL settings and demonstrate that it scales better, is more sample-efficient than prior methods, and outperforms baselines across several deep RL tasks.
